name: PAPUA N GUINEA

flag.title: Papua New Guinea
flag.note: Black & red halves, Bird of Paradise

lead: Papua New Guinea lies north of Australia on the world's second-largest island. Steep jungle mountains kept groups apart for centuries, so it has more languages than anywhere. Volcanoes rumble in the highlands.
geo: Jungle mountains called the Highlands form its spine. Valleys sit so high that frost forms at night. Rivers crash through rainforest to swampy coasts.
Hundreds of islands dot its seas, including New Britain and Bougainville. Active volcanoes like Tavurvur have buried whole towns in ash.
animals: The male Raggiana bird of paradise has flame-orange tail plumes and dances on a branch to impress females. Tree kangaroos bounce between branches high in the forest.
The Papuan taipan, one of the world's most venomous snakes, lurks in grasslands. Parrots, giant cassowaries and over 700 orchid species fill the forests.
culture: Papua New Guinea has over 800 living languages, more than any other country. Villages often cannot understand their neighbours, so people share Tok Pisin, a mix with English.
Sing-sings are huge festivals. Clans arrive in bright face paint and feathered headdresses to dance and feast. Each costume shows who the group is.
history: Humans reached New Guinea at least 50,000 years ago. Highland farmers grew taro and yams 10,000 years ago, inventing farming on their own.
Germany and Britain claimed parts of the island in 1884, and Australia took over after World War I. Papua New Guinea became independent on 16 September 1975.
wows: Over 800 languages are spoken by just 10 million people.
Highland farmers invented farming 10,000 years ago, like people in the Middle East.
Male birds of paradise hang upside down and shake their orange plumes.
Tavurvur volcano erupted in 1994 and buried the town of Rabaul in ash.
Tree kangaroos have padded paws that grip bark.
New Guinea is the world's second-largest island, shared with Indonesia.
Some villages stand on stilts over the sea, and children paddle between houses.

myths.fact: A cassowary has dagger-like claws about 12 cm long. It can kick hard.

myths.myth: Tok Pisin is just bad English
myths.fact: It is a real language with its own grammar. Its words come from English, German and local tongues.
